finding.claim: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object, so any authenticated user can set privileged or identity fields (role, isAdmin, id, tenantId, etc.) and persist them.
finding.source: req.body of PUT /me (users.js:4-5), attacker-controlled JSON from any authenticated user.
finding.sink: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) (users.js:5) followed by req.store.save(req.user) (users.js:6) and the response (users.js:7).

trace.note: Route handler for PUT /me; no field allowlist and no auth check in this file.
Object.assign copies every own key of req.body onto req.user with no filtering.
The mutated req.user is saved to the store as-is.
The full updated user object, including any fields the caller just set, is returned.

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist, no schema validation, and no role/owner check in users.js. req.user is assumed to be set by upstream auth middleware, which is not in this directory. Route-level auth is unknown. The store's save behavior (whether it keys on req.user.id and whether it persists arbitrary fields) is unknown.

verdict.guard_found: none. users.js:4-7 has no field allowlist, schema validation, or role/owner check. The only route-level auth would be upstream middleware, which is not in the directory (the only file is users.js). Its absence means req.user must come from elsewhere, so the caller is an authenticated user, not anonymous. The /me/profile handler at users.js:10-15 uses an allowlist, but that does not apply to /me.
verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no filtering, and users.js:6 saves the mutated object unchanged, so any caller who reaches PUT /me (req.user is set upstream, so this is an authenticated user) can overwrite any own property of their user record. Whether a privileged field such as role or isAdmin exists and is persisted depends on the user schema and store.save, which are not in this directory, so the privilege-escalation impact is a caveat, though the mass-assignment flaw itself is confirmed by the code shown.
